subject: Re: QuickCart – reported responses terminating mid-JSON (unable to reproduce)
messages:
From: Ari Weber <ari@quickcart.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Abrupt JSON termination seen in production responses

Hi Michael,

We're seeing some completions from Redwood's API that appear to terminate mid-JSON during normal traffic. Example: our server receives a partial object that ends with "...", then the connection closes. It's intermittent (~0.05% of requests) but causes downstream parsing failures for us. Attaching a small session snippet.

Can you confirm whether this is a server-side truncation or a client/transport issue? We haven't changed our client code.

Thanks,
Ari
Ari Weber
Engineering Manager, QuickCart

Attachment: qc-session-snippet-20261113.txt (text)
From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Ari Weber <ari@quickcart.com>, support@quickcart.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-13T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Abrupt JSON termination seen in production responses

Hi Ari — thanks for the snippet and the heads up.

Quick notes from initial triage:
- We reviewed the sample you attached and the session indicates the TCP connection was closed by the client shortly after receiving the last bytes.
- On our side we correlated request IDs from the sample against our intake logs and don't see an abrupt service-side stream termination; the tokens logged by the runtime indicate a normal end-of-stream (EOS) marker.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Could you share a full raw transcript (including your HTTP client/request logs and the exact request headers)? The snippet is helpful but appears truncated on the client side.
2) We'll run a focused reproduction against your request shape and model/parameters (please confirm model name and max_tokens).

I'll loop in Grace and Sean to run the reproductions and look for transport-layer anomalies.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Ari Weber <ari@quickcart.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T13:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Abrupt JSON termination seen in production responses

Thanks — I launched a reproduction suite using the same model (open-model-3-xl) and parameters Ari listed (temperature=0.0, max_tokens=512, stream=true). Over ~10k synthetic requests from our EU and US edge nodes we saw no mid-JSON terminations. All completions finished with a closing brace and proper EOS events.

I also checked our ingress proxies for any 499/connection-reset patterns tied to the request IDs — none correlated. Logs attached: redwood-run-log-20261113.json (subset).

If QuickCart can provide any raw client-level traces (curl/wget/http client) showing TCP FIN or RST, that will help narrow to client networking.

- Grace
Grace O'Connor
Platform Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ari Weber <ari@quickcart.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-14T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Abrupt JSON termination seen in production responses

Michael — thanks for running that. We dug into our side and found a short client bug: our HTTP client had a 10s idle-timeout for streaming responses due to a proxy change last month. When the model spent >10s generating (rare with long max_tokens), our proxy closed the connection which produced a partial payload at our end.

We also reproduced locally by artificially forcing a connection drop and saw the same truncated JSON. We're fixing the proxy timeout and will roll a patch tonight.

One ask: would Redwood consider returning a final event that includes an explicit stream-complete marker in the JSON payload before EOS? That would make parsing more robust for our use-case.

Appreciate the quick help.

—Ari
From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Ari Weber <ari@quickcart.com>, support@quickcart.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T17:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Abrupt JSON termination seen in production responses — closure

Ari — glad you found the proxy timeout and thanks for validating with a repro. Logging our final findings here so we can close the loop: 

Summary: Customer observed partial JSON objects due to client-side connection termination (proxy idle-timeout). Redwood runtime and edge logs show normal stream completion and EOS for correlated request IDs; no service-side truncation was observed.

Action items / recommendations:
- QuickCart: increase streaming idle timeout (or send periodic keep-alive/whitespace pings) to avoid mid-generation proxy closes. Patch rolling tonight sounds good.
- Redwood: we'll evaluate adding an optional 'stream_complete' sentinel event in the streaming protocol as a compatibility improvement. I've opened a ticket for product consideration: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/QC-5421.
- Both: if you see re-occurrence after the patch, re-open the ticket with a raw HTTP transcript and the associated request-id header.

Attachments: redwood-run-log-20261113.json (subset).

Closing the thread as "no service issue found" — happy to reopen if new evidence appears.

Best,
Michael Grant
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
